blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Reading a balance sheet with real understanding means looking for motion, not just totals. What has been growing on the asset side? What has been growing on the liability side? Where is working capital trending, and why? Is cash quietly falling while receivables have been building?

A balance sheet tells you where the company stands today, but it also reveals how it got there. A receivables balance that has been creeping up for three months means customers have been paying more slowly — which may be a collection problem, a quality problem, or an early warning that someone is in trouble.

The balance sheet is a snapshot that remembers the past. Read it carefully and it tells you more than any forecast about what next quarter is likely to look like.

items.q: According to the text, reading a balance sheet well means looking for…
items.why: "looking for motion, not just totals" — a leitura útil observa o movimento, não só os números finais.

items.q: What may a receivables balance that has been creeping up for three months indicate?
options: That the company has raised its prices
That customers have been paying more slowly
items.why: "customers have been paying more slowly" — o crescimento das contas a receber sinaliza pagamento mais lento.

items.q: The text calls the balance sheet "a snapshot that remembers the past." This suggests the author believes…
options: the balance sheet carries signals about how the company got there
the past is irrelevant to next quarter
the balance sheet is less useful than a forecast
the balance sheet only shows a single frozen moment
items.why: Inferência: "a snapshot that remembers the past" — a foto de hoje guarda o histórico que explica a trajetória.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A balance sheet can hint at next quarter
How a company got to its position matters
Rising receivables can be an early warning sign
A single total tells you everything you need to know
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta contra olhar só totais — o valor está no movimento, não num número isolado.

items.q: Why might the balance sheet reveal more than a forecast, according to the author?
options: Because it is prepared by more senior staff
Because it is updated every day
Because it records what has actually been happening, not a prediction
items.why: Inferência: "a snapshot that remembers the past" — baseia-se em fatos já ocorridos, ao contrário da previsão.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando o caso a um novo analista. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Look at these two quarters side by side. On paper, profit has been steady — almost flat, quarter after quarter. That is exactly why nobody raised a hand.

But watch the receivables line. It has been climbing for three months straight. Not a jump — a slow, quiet drift upwards. When I asked the sales team, they said everything was fine, the customers were happy. And they probably are happy. They have just been taking longer and longer to pay us.

Here is the part I want you to remember. The forecast never flagged this, because a forecast starts from the profit line, and the profit line looked healthy. The balance sheet flagged it, because cash has been falling at the same time the receivables have been rising. That gap is the whole story.

So next time someone tells you the quarter was steady, don't just trust the profit. Trace the working capital. If cash is draining while receivables build, something is moving underneath — and it usually shows up here months before it shows up anywhere else.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did nobody raise a concern at first?
options: Because profit had been steady, almost flat
Because the forecast was very optimistic
items.why: "profit has been steady — almost flat… That is exactly why nobody raised a hand."

items.q: What has been happening to the receivables line?
options: It has been climbing slowly for three months
It jumped suddenly in one month
It has been falling with cash
items.why: "It has been climbing for three months straight. Not a jump — a slow, quiet drift upwards."

items.q: Why did the forecast fail to flag the problem?
options: Because it was prepared too late
Because the sales team hid the data
Because it ignored the customers entirely
Because it starts from the profit line, which looked healthy
items.why: "a forecast starts from the profit line, and the profit line looked healthy."

items.q: When Sophie says "that gap is the whole story," she most likely means…
options: the missing pages in the report
the delay before the forecast was published
the gap between cash falling and receivables rising reveals the real problem
the difference between two accounting teams
items.why: Inferência: o descompasso entre caixa caindo e recebíveis subindo é justamente o sinal que denuncia o problema.

items.q: What lesson does Sophie want the analyst to take away?
options: Don't rely on profit alone — trace the working capital
Always trust the profit line above all else
Only the forecast can predict the next quarter
Cut the sales team out of the reporting process
items.why: Inferência: "don't just trust the profit. Trace the working capital." — o recado é olhar o movimento por baixo dos totais.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The numbers look fine, but there is real motion underneath." Here, motion means…
options: a formal proposal to vote on
the final total on the page
items.why: Motion = movimento: o que está mudando por baixo dos totais.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Cash tied up in unpaid invoices reduces the company's ___."
items.why: Working capital = capital de giro: o dinheiro disponível para o dia a dia, reduzido quando o caixa fica preso em recebíveis.

items.q: "Receivables have been creeping up for weeks." To creep up means to…
items.why: To creep up = subir silenciosamente, aos poucos, quase sem se notar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A rising receivables balance is often an ___ that a customer is in trouble."
items.why: Early warning = aviso precoce: sinal antecipado de um problema que ainda vai aparecer.

items.q: "A balance sheet is a snapshot of the company's position." A snapshot is…
options: a summary of the sales pipeline
a picture of a single moment in time
items.why: Snapshot = foto: retrata a posição da empresa num dado momento, não uma previsão.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on these figures." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "If receivables keep rising, we need to follow up with those customers." To follow up means to…
options: take further action to check or chase something
items.why: Follow up = dar sequência, cobrar ou verificar depois de um primeiro contato.

items.q: "Let's not gloss over the cash position." To gloss over means to…
options: treat something as unimportant or skip past it
items.why: Gloss over = passar por cima, tratar algo como se não importasse.

items.q: "A slow-paying customer can tie up a lot of cash." To tie up cash means to…
options: make it unavailable because it is committed elsewhere
items.why: Tie up (cash) = imobilizar o dinheiro, deixá-lo preso e indisponível.

items.q: "Trimming the total won't move the needle on liquidity." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
